    I will implement an optimized Nelder-Mead search algorithm modified to handle the inherent challenges of minimizing the evaluation function. 
    Starting from a normalized version of the parent sequence if available (if not, from smooth initializations), the approach will:
    1. Use gradient information to limit expensive evaluations (early_exit mechanism)
    2. Integrate active set gradient stepping tied to actual runtime
    3. Combine analytic bounds with direct function evaluations
    4. Maintain careful parent tracking and fallback mechanisms when the search appears to stall
    5. Reduce hyperparameter space through adaptive scheduling
    The goal is to lower the objective closer to 1.5027 by ensuring each function evaluation leverages genuine improvements rather than arbitrary parameter changes.
    
    Mathematical specification
    We minimize: 2*n*max(convolve(a,a))[k] / (sum(a))^2
    Where convolution is full mode: (n-1) + (n-1) + 1 = 2*n-1 coefficients.
    
    Steps:
    1. Read parent sequence and fall back to smooth initialization if none (normalized by simplex projection)
    2. Compute initial objective and gradient (with zero-avoidance modifications)
    3. Run Nelder-Mead with:
        • Target length around parent (if available) or adaptively chosen
        • Dynamic simplex size reduction on stall
        • Bandwidth interpolation maintenance
        • Gradient-guided insertions (more aggressive)
        • Improved exit conditions that preserve best candidate
    4. Verify improvement at every step before locking gradient on best candidate
    5. Return sequence along with best objective after evaluation

                    cols.append(j)
                    vals.append(a[i] * a[j])
